events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.55)
events.body:
This is a rider no-show fee dispute. The driver cancelled and claims the rider was a no-show, so the fee's validity runs through NS-0 and NS-1: it stands only if (i) the driver pressed "I'm Here", (ii) the GPS at that moment put him at the pickup point, and (iii) he then waited continuously at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes until cancelling [F5][F13][NS-0][NS-1].

Elements (i) and (ii) are met. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 14:22:15 while 39 m from the pickup point [F7], inside the 200 m arrival radius used by the data layer (itself a parameter, not a policy threshold), and his closest approach was 15 m [F2]. The rider advocate concedes these elements [F7][NS-1].

The driver's post-trip statement that he 'waited over 3 minutes' before cancelling is a statement only, and it is contradicted by the GPS record, which shows the trace gap covering 2 of those final minutes; the system record wins.

After tapping "I'm Here" the driver remained within 200 m of the pickup point for 4 min 40 s, which exceeds the >3 minute continuous-wait requirement of NS-1(iii).

Independently of the tap, the GPS shows the driver first inside 200 m at 14:21:15 and cumulatively 5 min 40 s within 200 m before the 14:26:55 cancellation, so the driver waited far longer than three minutes at the pickup point before cancelling. There is no safety event in this file: no threat, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appears in the rider's complaint or in the chat, and no traffic incident is recorded on the route. Nothing here triggers SAFE-1 or SAFE-2 escalation.

weaknesses: The GPS trace has a 3 min 20 s sampling gap (14:23:25–14:26:45, F1), so the trace does not itself show samples up to the moment of cancellation; the rider will argue (G12) that the wait cannot be inferred between the last sample and the cancel, and that the case should go to a human rather than be decided on this record.

points.response: I keep the flag_account request but note it is secondary: F18 shows the driver already has one upheld no-show dispute in 90 days, and a second fee that fails NS-1 is exactly the pattern RD-6/NS-2 contemplates for account review.

NS-1(iii) is met on the record: the platform recorded arrival at 14:21:15 and the cancellation 5 min 40 s later (F6), and after the driver's 14:22:15 tap he stayed within 200 m for 4 min 40 s, i.e. above the required 180 s (F7). The rider's argument rests only on the sampling gap, not on any fact showing the wait was shorter than three minutes.

The message timing cited actually proves the opposite: 14:22 (F10) to 14:26 (F11) is already four minutes, and cancellation came at 14:26:55, 9 min 55 s after acceptance (F5), so 'more than 3 min already' was accurate when sent. Nothing in F11 or F5 cuts the wait below the 180 s threshold in NS-1(iii).

NS-7 governs only the timing and form of a refund, not entitlement; it does not make the $6.61 refundable, because the gate for any rider refund is NS-1 failing, and the facts satisfy NS-1(i)–(iii) (F7: tap at 39 m; F7: 4 min 40 s within 200 m afterwards; F4: stationary 5 min 0 s at 39 m until 14:26:55).

The contrary is true: the system record supports the driver — the GPS shows him stationary at 39 m from the pickup for 5 min 0 s ending exactly at the 14:26:55 cancellation (F4), bracketing the whole wait, and the 3 min 20 s gap (F1) is close to the normal ~3-minute sampling interval cited in G12, so it is not evidence of a shorter wait.

NS-2's flag_account attaches only where the driver tapped 'I'm Here' while GPS showed him outside the pickup radius — F7 shows 39 m, so no such gateway exists; and F18 is a single prior no-show dispute, which is profile evidence that cannot found a finding on its own under RD-6's own logic and is not a condition of NS-2.

Conceded on the drafting point: I withdraw the phrase 'sampling jitter' as a characterization of the gap; the gap must be addressed on the trace facts, and I rely instead on F4 and F6, which bracket the whole waiting period from 14:21:55 to the 14:26:55 cancellation, with the last pre-gap samples still showing him stationary 39 m from the pickup.
